pages.title: Author Guidelines
pages.html:
Author Guidelines

The Journal of Academic Tourism Analysis (Journal ATA) is an international, double-blind peer-reviewed academic journal operating under a Diamond Open Access model. It is dedicated to advancing original scientific knowledge in tourism and related disciplines. Submitted manuscripts must be original, previously unpublished, and not currently under consideration elsewhere. Furthermore, submission implies that all co-authors have approved the final content and consent to the journal's publication policies.

Article Types

Journal ATA accepts the following types of articles:

  • Research Article: Empirical studies offering original data, original analysis, and scientific contribution.

  • Review Article: Studies that systematically or critically evaluate the existing literature on a specific topic.

  • Conceptual Article: Studies that develop new conceptual models or critically discuss existing theories.

  • Methodological Article: Studies presenting innovations regarding research methods, analytical techniques, or measurement tools.

(Note: Research notes, book reviews, article/book critiques, and academic opinions are accepted only with editorial approval and/or invitation.)

Publication Priorities and Evaluation Criteria

All submissions to Journal ATA are expected to meet high academic standards in terms of scientific originality, ethical research principles, methodological rigor, and theoretical contribution.

Priority is Given to Studies That:

  • Provide an original theoretical contribution to the tourism literature.

  • Develop new conceptual models or critically re-evaluate existing theories.

  • Have a strong research design.

  • Employ quantitative, qualitative, or mixed methods in accordance with scientific standards.

  • Develop an interdisciplinary perspective.

  • Provide scientific solutions to current tourism issues.

  • Hold the potential to contribute to the international literature.

  • Offer concrete implications for tourism practices.

Studies with a High Probability of Desk Rejection: The Editor-in-Chief or Section Editor may directly reject studies that do not meet the following criteria without initiating the peer-review process:

  • Purely descriptive research offering no theoretical contribution.

  • Studies with an insufficient literature base.

  • Studies where scientific research methods are not clearly explained.

  • Studies that merely report findings instead of providing an analytical evaluation.

  • Situation assessments lacking scientific discussion.

  • Research with an insufficient sample or data foundation.

  • Research lacking ethics committee approval when required.

  • Studies that fail to comply with scientific writing rules and the journal template.

  • Studies with a similarity rate above the acceptable limit.

  • Studies falling outside the aims and scope of the journal.

Article Preparation and Formatting Rules

General Format and Template Usage:

  • All manuscripts must be written in Microsoft Word using the "Journal ATA Article Template". The formatting settings within the template must not be altered. Manuscripts will be returned to the authors if the template is not used or if required files are missing.

  • Rules regarding fonts, formatting principles, tables, figures, footnotes, equations, citations, and the reference list must be strictly followed as specified in the article template.

  • Author information must not be included in the main text. This information must be provided in the "Title Page" submitted among the application files.

Language and Word Limits:

  • Manuscripts can be written in Turkish or English. Regardless of the language, both a Turkish Öz and an English Abstract must be provided. (Free support is provided by the journal secretariat to non-Turkish speaking authors for the preparation of the Turkish Öz).

  • The word count of the manuscript should be between 4000–7000 words at the initial submission. Following the peer-review and revision process, the final text must not exceed 8000 words (including tables, figures, and references). Non-compliance with word limits is grounds for return.

  • Extensive Summary: For all manuscripts written in Turkish, an "Extensive Summary" of 800–1200 words must be prepared after the "References" section. When preparing this summary, either American or British English must be used consistently; the two should not be mixed.

  • The manuscript must be written in clear, consistent, academic, and objective language. Unnecessary repetitions, subjective expressions, and unscientific discourse must be avoided.

Article Sections and Content Principles

Empirical studies should sequentially consist of the following sections: Introduction, Literature Review, Methodology, Findings, Discussion, Conclusion, and References. Depending on the nature of the manuscript, this structure may be modified in line with editorial evaluation.

  • Title: Should be clear, original, concise, and reflect the main contribution of the research. Abbreviations should be avoided.

  • Abstract: Should briefly and clearly present the purpose, method, main findings, scientific contribution, and conclusions of the study, and must be maximum 200 words (between 150-200 words). No citations should be made within the abstract.

  • Keywords: Must be at least 3 and at most 5. General, plural, and multiple concepts (e.g., using "and", "/") should be avoided. American or British English must be used consistently. Abbreviations should not be used (unless widely accepted in the literature).

  • Introduction: Subheadings must not be used in this section.

  • Literature Review: Must be prepared with a current, international, critical, and theoretical perspective. Merely listing sources is not sufficient; authors are expected to synthesize existing knowledge to reveal the research gap.

  • Methodology: The research design, population and sample, data collection method, data analysis process, and validity/reliability issues must be explained clearly enough to ensure replicability. Furthermore, the following two issues must be mandatorily addressed in this section:

    • Ethics Committee Status: If ethics committee approval was obtained for the research, the institution/committee granting the approval, the date, and the document/decision number must be stated. If ethics committee approval is not required, the reason for this (e.g., use of public data, no human/animal subjects) must be clearly justified.

    • AI Usage: If generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools were utilized during the research, analysis, or writing process, the exact purpose of their use (e.g., translation, proofreading, data analysis) must be clearly stated. If AI was not used, no declaration is required.

  • Findings: Should only present the research results. Interpretations must be reserved for the discussion section. Tables and figures should be used without creating unnecessary repetition.

  • Discussion: Findings should be compared with the existing literature, theoretical contributions explained, reasons for differences discussed, and the original contribution of the research demonstrated.

  • Conclusion: Main inferences, theoretical contributions, practical implications, limitations of the research, and recommendations for future research must be presented under separate subheadings.

  • References: Must be prepared in strict accordance with the APA 7 system adopted by the journal. Every in-text citation must appear in the reference list, and every reference listed must be cited in the text. Authors should utilize current and international sources as much as possible.

Ethical Principles, Transparency, and Similarity (Plagiarism) Check

  • Similarity (Plagiarism) Check: Every submitted manuscript undergoes a similarity check. Authors can obtain a similarity report via DergiPark or intihal.net. The acceptable similarity rate is maximum 20%, excluding references.

  • Ethics Declaration and Committee Approval: Regardless of the nature of the research, all authors are required to complete the journal's "Ethics Declaration" form and include it with their submission documents. However, for research involving human participants (using methods such as surveys, interviews, observations), an official Ethics Committee Approval must also be obtained. The fact that the research was conducted according to ethical standards and whether Ethics Committee Approval was required must also be declared in the methodology section of the manuscript.

  • Authorship Declaration: Everyone listed as an author must have made a significant scientific contribution to the study. Honorary, ghost, and purchased authorships are unacceptable. Stating contributions according to the CRediT (Contributor Roles Taxonomy) system is encouraged.

  • Conflict of Interest: All authors must explicitly declare any financial, institutional, or personal conflicts of interest that could influence the study. The absence of a conflict of interest must also be stated in the manuscript.

  • Funding Declaration: If the research was supported by any institution/organization, the funding details must be fully disclosed.

  • Data Sharing: Authors are expected to securely store their data; where possible, making the data accessible to support scientific verifiability is encouraged.

  • AI Usage: AI tools may be used as assisting instruments but cannot be listed as authors. If generative AI technologies were substantially utilized, this must be explicitly declared in the manuscript. All scientific and ethical responsibility lies with the authors.

Required Documents at Submission

The following mandatory documents must be included with the submission. If missing files are uploaded, the manuscript will be returned to the authors for correction before the evaluation process begins.

Article Templates:

  • 📝 Journal ATA Article Template (For English Article)  

  • 📝 Journal ATA Article Template (For Turkish Article)   

Application and Declaration Forms:

  • 📝 Title Page (This is the only document containing author information; authors are responsible for accurately filling in the details.)

  • 📝 Authorship Contribution Statement

  • 📝 Declaration of Competing Interest 

  • 📝 Ethical Statement

  • 📝 Copyright Agreement

  • 📝 Support and Acknowledgment Statement

  • 📝 Disclaimer of Authorship (Required only in the event of an author being removed from the study.)

Reports and Official Permission Documents:

  • 📄 Ethics Committee Approval Document (An official committee approval required for studies employing methods such as surveys/interviews, depending on the nature of the research.)

  • 📊 Similarity (Plagiarism) Report (A report showing a maximum similarity rate of 20%, excluding references.(

Final Pre-Submission Checklist

Before submitting your manuscript, please verify the following:

  • The study is original.

  • It is not currently under review by another journal.

  • All authors have approved the submission.

  • Ethics committee information has been added (under the methodology heading).

  • Conflict of interest declaration is included.

  • Funding information is specified.

  • Author contributions have been prepared.

  • Data sharing declaration is included.

  • AI usage declaration has been prepared (if applicable).

  • The manuscript complies with the formatting and writing rules.

  • The reference list has been verified against APA 7.

  • A similarity check has been conducted (<20%).

  • The manuscript aligns with the aims and scope of Journal ATA.

Last Update Time: 09 November 2026

Yazım Kuralları

Akademik Turizm Analizi Dergisine (Journal ATA), turizm ve ilişkili disiplinlerde özgün bilimsel bilgi üretimine katkı sağlayan, Elmas Açık Erişim (Diamond Open Access) modeliyle yayın yapan, uluslararası ve çift kör hakemli akademik bir dergidir. Dergiye gönderilen çalışmalar daha önce herhangi bir yerde yayımlanmamış, yayımlanmak üzere değerlendirme sürecinde bulunmayan ve tüm yazarlar tarafından onaylanmış özgün çalışmalar olmalıdır. Makalenin dergiye gönderilmesi, tüm yazarların çalışmanın içeriğini onayladığı ve derginin yayın politikalarını kabul ettiği anlamına gelir.

Makale Türleri

Journal ATA, aşağıdaki makale türlerini kabul etmektedir:

  • Araştırma Makalesi: Özgün veri, özgün analiz ve bilimsel katkı sunan ampirik çalışmalar.

  • Derleme Makalesi: Belirli bir konuda mevcut literatürü sistematik veya eleştirel biçimde değerlendiren çalışmalar.

  • Kavramsal Makale: Yeni kuramsal modeller geliştiren veya mevcut teorileri eleştirel biçimde tartışan çalışmalar.

  • Metodolojik Makale: Araştırma yöntemleri, analiz teknikleri veya ölçüm araçlarına ilişkin yenilik sunan çalışmalar.

(Not: Araştırma notu, kitap incelemesi, makale/kitap eleştirisi ve akademik görüş türündeki çalışmalar yalnızca editör onayı ve/veya daveti ile kabul edilmektedir.)

Derginin Yayın Öncelikleri ve Değerlendirme Kriterleri

Dergiye gönderilen tüm çalışmaların bilimsel özgünlük, etik araştırma ilkeleri, metodolojik titizlik ve kuramsal katkı açısından yüksek akademik standartları karşılaması beklenmektedir.

Derginin Öncelik Verdiği Çalışmalar:

  • Turizm literatürüne özgün kuramsal katkı sağlayan,

  • Yeni kavramsal modeller geliştiren veya mevcut kuramları eleştirel biçimde yeniden değerlendiren,

  • Güçlü araştırma tasarımına sahip,

  • Nicel, nitel veya karma yöntemleri bilimsel standartlara uygun biçimde kullanan,

  • Disiplinler arası bakış açısı geliştiren,

  • Güncel turizm sorunlarına bilimsel çözümler sunan,

  • Uluslararası literatüre katkı potansiyeli taşıyan,

  • Turizm uygulamalarına yönelik somut çıkarımlar sunan çalışmalar.

Doğrudan Reddedilme (Desk Rejection) Olasılığı Yüksek Çalışmalar: Baş Editör veya Alan Editörü aşağıdaki ölçütleri karşılamayan çalışmaları hakem sürecine göndermeden doğrudan reddedebilir:

  • Kuramsal katkı sunmayan yalnızca betimleyici araştırmalar,

  • Yetersiz literatür temeline sahip çalışmalar,

  • Bilimsel araştırma yöntemleri açık şekilde açıklanmayan çalışmalar,

  • Analitik değerlendirme yerine yalnızca bulgu aktaran çalışmalar,

  • Bilimsel tartışma içermeyen durum tespitleri,

  • Yetersiz örneklem veya veri temeline sahip araştırmalar,

  • Etik kurul gerektirdiği hâlde etik kurul izni bulunmayan araştırmalar,

  • Bilimsel yazım kurallarına ve makale şablonuna uymayan çalışmalar,

  • Benzerlik oranı kabul edilebilir sınırların üzerinde olan çalışmalar,

  • Derginin amaç ve kapsamı dışında kalan çalışmalar.

Makale Hazırlama ve Biçimsel Kurallar

Genel Biçim ve Şablon Kullanımı:

  • Tüm çalışmalar Microsoft Word programında “Journal ATA Makale Şablonu” kullanılarak yazılmalıdır. Dergi şablonunda yer alan biçimsel düzenlemeler kesinlikle değiştirilmemelidir. Şablonun kullanılmadığı veya eksik dosya yüklendiği tespit edildiğinde çalışma yazarlara iade edilir.

  • Yazı tipi, biçimlendirme esasları, tablo, şekil, dipnot, denklem kullanımı ile atıf ve kaynakça düzenine ilişkin kurallara makale şablonunda belirtilen şekilde uyulmalıdır.

  • Yazar bilgilerine çalışma metni içerisinde yer verilmemelidir. Bu bilgiler için başvuru dosyaları arasında yer alan “Başlık Sayfası” eksiksiz şekilde doldurulmalıdır.

Dil ve Kelime Sınırları:

  • Çalışma Türkçe ya da İngilizce dilinde yazılabilir. Çalışmanın dili ne olursa olsun, Türkçe Öz ve İngilizce Abstract birlikte sunulmalıdır. (Türkçe bilmeyen yazarlara, Türkçe Öz hazırlanması konusunda dergi sekretaryası tarafından ücretsiz destek sağlanmaktadır).

  • Çalışmanın kelime sayısı ilk gönderimde 4000–7000 kelime arasında olmalı; hakem değerlendirme ve revizyon süreci sonrasında nihai metin en fazla 8000 kelimeyi aşmamalıdır (tablolar, şekiller ve kaynakça dâhil). Sınırlara uyulmaması iade sebebidir.

  • Genişletilmiş Özet (Extensive Summary): Türkçe yazılmış tüm çalışmalarda, “Kaynakça” bölümünden sonra “Extensive Summary” başlığı altında 800–1200 kelime arasında genişletilmiş bir özet hazırlanmalıdır. Hazırlanırken Amerikan veya Britanya İngilizcesinden biri esas alınmalı; iki kullanım bir arada olmamalıdır.

  • Makale; açık, tutarlı, akademik ve nesnel bir dille yazılmalıdır. Gereksiz tekrarlar, öznel ifadeler ve bilimsel olmayan söylemlerden kaçınılmalıdır.

Makale Bölümleri ve İçerik İlkeleri

Ampirik çalışmalar sırasıyla; Giriş, Yazın İncelemesi, Yöntem, Bulgular, Sonuç ve Kaynakça bölümlerinden oluşmalıdır. Makalenin niteliğine göre bu yapı editöryal değerlendirme doğrultusunda değiştirilebilir.

  • Başlık: Açık, özgün, kısa ve araştırmanın temel katkısını yansıtan nitelikte olmalıdır. Kısaltma kullanılmaması tercih edilir.

  • Öz: Çalışmanın amacı, yöntemi, temel bulguları, bilimsel katkısı ve sonuçları kısa/açık biçimde sunulmalı ve en fazla 200 sözcükten oluşmalıdır (150-200 kelime arası). Öz içerisinde kaynak gösterimi yapılmamalıdır.

  • Anahtar Kelimeler: En az 3, en fazla 5 adet olmalıdır. Genel, çoğul ve çoklu kavramlardan (örneğin “ve”, “/” vb.) kaçınılmalıdır. İngilizce kelimelerde Amerikan veya Britanya İngilizcesi tutarlı biçimde kullanılmalıdır. Kısaltma kullanılmamalıdır (yalnızca literatürde yaygın kabul görmüş kısaltmalar hariç).

  • Giriş: Giriş bölümünde alt başlık kullanılmamalıdır.

  • Literatür (Yazın İncelemesi): Güncel, uluslararası, eleştirel ve kuramsal bir bakış açısıyla hazırlanmalıdır. Kaynakların yalnızca sıralanması yeterli değildir; mevcut bilgi birikimi sentezlenerek araştırmanın bilgi boşluğu ortaya konmalıdır.

  • Yöntem: Araştırma deseni, araştırma nüfusu ve örneklem, veri toplama yöntemi, veri analiz süreci, geçerlik ve güvenilirlik konuları araştırmanın tekrarlanabilirliğini sağlayacak düzeyde açıklanmalıdır. Ayrıca bu bölümde şu iki hususa zorunlu olarak yer verilmelidir:

    • Etik Kurul Durumu: Araştırma için etik kurul izni alınmışsa; iznin hangi kurum veya kuruldan, hangi tarih ve belge/karar numarası ile alındığı yazılmalıdır. Eğer çalışma için etik kurul izni gerekmiyorsa, izne neden gerek duyulmadığı (örneğin; veri setinin halka açık olması, insan/hayvan denek içermemesi vb.) açıkça gerekçelendirilmelidir.

    • Yapay Zekâ Kullanımı: Araştırma, analiz veya yazım sürecinde üretken yapay zekâ (AI) araçlarından yararlanılmışsa, bu araçların tam olarak hangi amaçla (örneğin; çeviri, dil düzeltmesi, veri analizi, vb.) kullanıldığı açıkça belirtilmelidir. Yapay zeka kullanılmadıysa ayrıca beyana gerek yoktur.

  • Bulgular: Yalnızca araştırma sonuçlarını sunmalıdır. Yorumlar, tartışma bölümünde yapılmalıdır. Tablo ve şekiller gereksiz tekrar oluşturmayacak biçimde kullanılmalıdır.

  • Tartışma: Bulgular mevcut literatürle karşılaştırılmalı, kuramsal katkılar açıklanmalı, farklılıkların nedenleri tartışılmalı ve araştırmanın özgün katkısı ortaya konulmalıdır.

  • Sonuç: Temel çıkarımlar, kuramsal katkılar, uygulamaya yönelik öneriler, araştırmanın sınırlılıkları ve gelecek araştırmalara yönelik öneriler ayrı alt başlıklar altında sunulmalıdır.

  • Kaynakça: Kaynaklar derginin benimsediği APA 7 sistemine eksiksiz uygun hazırlanmalıdır. Her metin içi atfın kaynakçada yer alması ve her kaynakça kaydının metin içerisinde kullanılmış olması zorunludur. Güncel ve uluslararası kaynaklardan yararlanılmalıdır.

Etik İlkeler, Şeffaflık ve Benzerlik (İntihal) Denetimi

  • Benzerlik (İntihal) Denetimi: Gönderilen her çalışma benzerlik denetiminden geçirilmektedir. Yazarlar, DergiPark veya intihal.net üzerinden benzerlik raporu alabilir. Kabul edilebilir benzerlik oranı kaynakça hariç %20'dir.

  • Etik Beyan ve Kurul Onayı: Araştırmanın niteliği ne olursa olsun, tüm yazarların derginin "Etik Beyan" formunu doldurup başvuru belgeleri arasına eklemesi zorunludur. Bununla birlikte; insan katılımcılar üzerinde yürütülen (anket, mülakat, gözlem vb. yöntemlerin kullanıldığı) araştırmalar için ayrıca resmi Etik Kurul İzni alınmış olması şarttır. Araştırmanın etik standartlara uygun yürütüldüğü, Etik Kurul İzni gerekip gerekmediği bilgisi makalenin yöntemi içerisinde de beyan edilmelidir.

  • Yazarlık Beyanı: Yazar olarak belirtilen herkes çalışmaya önemli bilimsel katkı sağlamış olmalıdır. Onursal, hayalet ve satın alınmış yazarlık kabul edilmez. Katkıların CRediT (Contributor Roles Taxonomy) sistemine uygun belirtilmesi teşvik edilir.

  • Çıkar Çatışması: Tüm yazarlar, çalışmayı etkileyebilecek finansal, kurumsal veya kişisel çıkar çatışmalarını açıkça beyan etmek zorundadır. Çıkar çatışması bulunmaması durumunda da bu durum makalede belirtilmelidir.

  • Finansman Beyanı: Araştırma herhangi bir kurum/kuruluş tarafından desteklenmişse eksiksiz olarak belirtilmelidir.

  • Veri Paylaşımı: Yazarların veriyi güvenli şekilde saklamaları beklenir; mümkünse verinin bilimsel doğrulanabilirliği destekleyecek şekilde erişilebilir olması teşvik edilir.

  • Yapay Zekâ Kullanımı: Yapay zekâ araçları yardımcı araç olarak kullanılabilir ancak yazar olarak gösterilemez. Üretken yapay zekâ teknolojilerinden önemli ölçüde yararlanılmışsa bu durum makalede açıkça beyan edilmelidir. Tüm bilimsel/etik sorumluluk yazarlara aittir.

Başvuru Aşamasında İstenen Belgeler

Aşağıda yer alan zorunlu belgelerin başvuruya eklenmesi gerekmektedir. Eksik dosya yüklendiğinde, sürece başlanmadan önce düzeltilip yeniden gönderilmesi amacıyla çalışma yazarlara iade edilir.

Makale Şablonları:

  • 📝 Journal ATA Makale Şablonu (İngilizce makaleler için) 

  • 📝 Journal ATA Makale Şablonu (Türkçe makaleler için)

Başvuru ve Beyan Formları:

  • 📝 Başlık Sayfası (Yazar bilgilerinin yer aldığı tek belgedir; bilgilerin doğru doldurulmasından yazarlar sorumludur.)

  • 📝 Yazarlık Katkı Beyanı 

  • 📝 Çıkar Çatışması Beyanı

  • 📝 Etik Beyan

  • 📝 Telif Sözleşmesi 

  • 📝 Destek ve Teşekkür Beyanı

  • 📝 Yazarlık Feragatnamesi (Bir yazarın çalışmadan çıkarılması durumunda)

Rapor ve Resmi İzin Belgeleri:

  • 📄 Etik Kurul Onayı Belgesi (Araştırmanın niteliğine bağlı olarak, anket/mülakat gibi yöntemlerin kullanıldığı çalışmalar için zorunlu olan resmi kurul onayıdır.)

  • 📊 Benzerlik (İntihal) Raporu (Kaynakça hariç en fazla %20 benzerlik oranını gösteren rapor.)

Makale Gönderim Öncesi Son Kontrol Listesi

Makalenizi göndermeden önce aşağıdaki hususları kontrol ediniz:

  • Çalışma özgündür.

  • Başka bir dergide değerlendirme sürecinde değildir.

  • Tüm yazarlar gönderimi onaylamıştır.

  • Etik kurul bilgisi eklenmiştir (yöntem başlığı altında).

  • Çıkar çatışması beyanı eklenmiştir.

  • Finansman bilgisi belirtilmiştir.

  • Yazar katkıları hazırlanmıştır.

  • Veri paylaşım beyanı eklenmiştir.

  • Yapay zekâ kullanım beyanı hazırlanmıştır (gerekiyorsa).

  • Makale yazım kurallarına uygundur.

  • Kaynakça kontrol edilmiştir.

  • Benzerlik kontrolü yapılmıştır.

  • Makale, derginin amaç ve kapsamına uygundur.

pages.title: Ethical Principles and Publication Policy
pages.html:
Ethical Principles and Publication Policy

Ethical Principles

The Journal of Academic Tourism Analysis (Journal ATA) is committed to the principles of integrity, impartiality, transparency, accountability, and academic freedom in scholarly publishing. The Journal considers research integrity, the independence of editorial decisions, the fairness of peer review, and the reliability of the scholarly record to be among its fundamental responsibilities.

In developing its ethical principles, the Journal takes into consideration the RESPECT Code of Practice for socio-economic research, the Principles of Transparency and Best Practice in Scholarly Publishing, the Core Practices published by the Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE), the Singapore Statement on Research Integrity, and the Recommendations for the Conduct, Reporting, Editing, and Publication of Scholarly Work published by the International Committee of Medical Journal Editors (ICMJE). ICMJE recommendations are applied, where relevant, with due regard to the characteristics of tourism research and the applicable legal and ethical framework.

The Journal's publishing processes are conducted in accordance with applicable legislation in Türkiye, the Council of Higher Education's Directive on Scientific Research and Publication Ethics, and other relevant ethical regulations, depending on the nature of the research.

The Journal addresses plagiarism, fabrication, falsification, duplicate publication, inappropriate authorship practices, undisclosed conflicts of interest, false declarations of ethical approval, and other practices that may undermine the integrity of scholarly research. Allegations of ethical misconduct are assessed impartially, confidentially, and proportionately, taking into account the nature of the allegation and the available evidence.

Responsibilities of the Journal

Journal ATA is responsible for protecting the integrity of scholarly publishing and maintaining a fair publishing environment for all participants. In this context, the Journal:

  • Publishes clear and accessible policies concerning its publishing processes, peer-review model, authorship criteria, fee policy, open-access conditions, licensing, conflicts of interest, and procedures for addressing ethical concerns.

  • Ensures that editorial decisions are based on scholarly merit, originality, methodological adequacy, relevance to the Journal's scope, and the contribution of the work.

  • Requires the disclosure and appropriate management of conflicts of interest involving authors, reviewers, editors, and other participants in the publishing process.

  • Supports the independent conduct of scholarly inquiry, critical evaluation, and academic debate without inappropriate personal, institutional, or commercial influence.

  • Protects the confidentiality of submitted manuscripts and peer-review reports and takes appropriate care to protect personal data and information relating to research participants.

  • Maintains digital archiving practices intended to support the long-term accessibility of published work and the integrity of the scholarly record.

  • Investigates concerns relating to research and publication ethics and may request explanations or supporting documentation from authors, reviewers, editors, or relevant institutions where necessary.

  • Takes appropriate post-publication action, including issuing corrections, expressions of concern, or retractions, when a published work is found to contain errors or information that may compromise the reliability of the scholarly record.

  • Promotes transparency, accuracy, confidentiality, and human accountability in the use of artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted tools.

Responsibilities of Editors

Editors are responsible for assessing the scholarly and ethical suitability of submitted manuscripts and ensuring that editorial decisions are made fairly.

Editors:

  • Make editorial decisions on the basis of the manuscript's scholarly quality and the Journal's publication criteria, rather than the authors' identity, institutional affiliation, personal relationships, political views, or commercial interests.

  • Conduct an initial assessment of manuscripts in terms of scope, originality, methodology, ethical suitability, and scholarly contribution. The decision to send a manuscript for peer review or to decline it at the initial stage is made within the scope of editorial responsibility.

  • Recuse themselves from editorial handling when a conflict of interest exists and, where necessary, assign the manuscript to an independent editor.

  • Select reviewers by considering subject expertise, independence, competence, and potential conflicts of interest.

  • Evaluate reviewer reports on their scholarly merits and may seek additional reviews when substantial differences arise between reviewers' assessments.

  • Retain responsibility for the final editorial decision while taking reviewers' recommendations into consideration.

  • Maintain the confidentiality of authors' and reviewers' identities, submitted manuscripts, review reports, and editorial correspondence.

  • Make reasonable efforts to process manuscripts in a timely manner and keep authors informed about the progress of the review process.

  • Investigate allegations of ethical misconduct impartially, considering the explanations of the parties involved and the available evidence. Allegations are not treated as established misconduct solely on the basis of suspicion.

  • Where necessary, request information or an investigation from the institution where the research was conducted or from the relevant ethics committee or competent authority.

  • Take appropriate action when plagiarism, fabrication, falsification, duplicate publication, inappropriate authorship, or other ethical misconduct is identified.

  • Ensure that appropriate post-publication action is taken when a published article contains significant errors or raises concerns about research integrity.

  • Facilitate the consideration of scholarly criticism, correction requests, and ethical complaints concerning published work.

Editors must not participate in decisions concerning their own manuscripts, submissions from close colleagues or relatives, or other cases in which personal or professional interests may compromise their impartiality. Whenever possible, such submissions are handled by an independent editor.

Responsibilities of Reviewers

Peer review is an independent evaluation process intended to improve the quality and reliability of scholarly work. Reviewers are expected to act impartially, maintain confidentiality, exercise appropriate expertise, and provide constructive criticism.

Reviewers:

  • Assess whether the subject falls within their expertise, whether they can complete the review within the required timeframe, and whether any potential conflict of interest exists before accepting an invitation.

  • Inform the editor and decline the invitation when they lack the necessary expertise or cannot provide an impartial assessment.

  • Evaluate manuscripts in terms of originality, theoretical contribution, methodological adequacy, consistency of data and findings, use of sources, and the justification of conclusions.

  • Provide clear, objective, reasoned, and constructive comments. Criticism must address the scholarly content rather than the individuals involved.

  • Submit their reports within the agreed timeframe and provide specific recommendations that may help improve the manuscript.

  • Refrain from using unpublished information, data, or ideas obtained during peer review for their own research or for the benefit of third parties.

  • Maintain the confidentiality of manuscripts, supplementary files, and correspondence relating to the review process.

  • Inform the editor, with appropriate justification, if they suspect plagiarism, inappropriate citation, fabrication, falsification, duplicate publication, or other ethical concerns.

  • Avoid bias based on authors' identities, institutional affiliations, countries, language, or personal characteristics.

  • Obtain the editor's permission before seeking assistance from another expert and disclose that person's contribution where applicable.

  • Refrain from uploading confidential or unpublished manuscript content to AI tools or third-party systems unless the Journal has explicitly permitted such use and adequate confidentiality safeguards are in place.

  • Follow the Journal's policies when using AI-assisted tools for review and critically assess any output for possible errors, omissions, or bias.

Reviewers are not automatically required to decline a manuscript solely because they have reviewed an earlier version for another journal. However, they must inform the editor if the previous review creates a confidentiality concern, a conflict of interest, or a risk to their independence, and withdraw when necessary.

Responsibilities of Authors

Authors are responsible for the originality, scientific accuracy, ethical integrity, and completeness of the work they submit for publication.

Authors:

  • Conduct and report their research honestly, transparently, and in accordance with the principles of research integrity and reproducibility.

  • Properly acknowledge and cite the ideas, statements, data, images, and other materials of others and comply with applicable permission and licensing requirements.

  • Accurately describe the theoretical foundations, methodology, data, findings, and limitations of their work. They must not fabricate, falsify, or misleadingly present data.

  • Disclose whether the manuscript has previously been published or is under consideration elsewhere. The same manuscript must not be submitted to more than one journal simultaneously.

  • Obtain ethical approval, research permissions, informed consent, and other required documentation when warranted by the nature of the research and applicable regulations.

  • Comply with ethical principles and legal requirements concerning human participants, vulnerable groups, animals, and personal data.

  • Disclose financial and non-financial conflicts of interest, funding sources, and relationships that may influence the research or its interpretation.

  • Ensure that all individuals who meet the authorship criteria are appropriately credited and that contributors who do not meet those criteria are acknowledged where appropriate.

  • Determine authorship order transparently and on the basis of the authors' actual contributions and mutual agreement.

  • Verify the accuracy of data, analyses, references, and figures and inform the editor of significant errors or ethical concerns identified after publication.

  • Respond to editorial and reviewer comments with reasoned explanations and complete requested revisions within the specified timeframe, where reasonably possible.

  • Cooperate with the Journal in investigations concerning the reliability or ethical integrity of their work, both during and after publication.

Authors retain ultimate responsibility for the content and accuracy of their work. The use of AI-assisted tools does not diminish this responsibility.

Authorship and Contributions

Authorship must be based on actual scholarly contributions to the work. Journal ATA promotes transparency in authorship and contributor statements. The ICMJE authorship criteria are considered a guiding framework in this regard.

Authorship requires a substantial contribution to the conception or design of the work, or to the acquisition, analysis, or interpretation of data; participation in drafting the manuscript or critically revising it for important intellectual content; approval of the final version to be published; and agreement to be accountable for all aspects of the work. These criteria must be considered together.

General supervision, administrative support, funding acquisition, language editing alone, or data collection alone does not automatically justify authorship in the absence of other substantial scholarly contributions and the required authorship responsibilities.

Authors' contributions must be stated clearly in the format required by the Journal. Ghost authorship, guest authorship, honorary authorship, and the exclusion of individuals who qualify for authorship are not acceptable.

The order of authorship must be determined by mutual agreement among the authors. Rather than arbitrating authorship disputes, editors may request explanations and supporting documentation and, when the dispute cannot be resolved, recommend that the matter be referred to the relevant institution for investigation.

Requests to add, remove, or reorder authors must be supported by a clear explanation. Written agreement must be obtained from all existing authors and from any individual being added or removed. The editor evaluates whether the proposed change is ethically and procedurally appropriate. Changes requested after acceptance are considered only after the reasons and necessary approvals have been verified.

Authorship of Articles Derived from Theses

For articles derived from postgraduate theses, authorship is determined on the basis of actual scholarly contributions, the applicable authorship criteria, and relevant regulations, rather than solely on the basis of supervisory relationships or academic titles.

A student who meets the authorship criteria through their contribution to the scientific content and preparation of the article must be credited as an author. Supervisors may also qualify for authorship according to their contributions and fulfilment of the relevant responsibilities. Supervision alone does not automatically establish authorship, and the supervisory relationship must not be used to deny a student an authorship credit to which they are entitled.

For thesis-derived articles, authorship order, contributions, and responsibilities should be determined transparently by the parties involved. Where a waiver of authorship or an authorship dispute arises, written statements from the parties and the rules of the relevant institution will be taken into consideration. A waiver does not replace the ethical responsibilities associated with actual contributions and authorship criteria.

Research Ethics, Ethical Approval, and Informed Consent

Authors must conduct research in accordance with applicable legislation, the ethical standards of the relevant discipline, and the requirements appropriate to the nature of the research.

For research involving human participants, personal data, vulnerable groups, or animals, the necessary ethics committee approvals and other permissions must be obtained where required by applicable regulations and the nature of the study. Research that requires ethical approval but has not obtained it will not be accepted for publication. If an exemption applies, the authors must explain the reason and, where available, provide documentation from the relevant institution.

Authors must state the name of the ethics committee, the approval date, and the approval or protocol number in the manuscript. Where ethical approval is not required, the reasons must be clearly explained. The editor may request an approval document or further clarification where necessary.

Informed consent must be obtained from research participants in a manner appropriate to the study. Participants' voluntary involvement, privacy, protection of personal data, and right to withdraw from the research must be respected. Necessary permissions must be obtained before publishing identifiable images, personal information, or other materials relating to individuals. Anonymisation must be sufficient to prevent the identification of participants.

Animal research must comply with applicable legislation and the requirements of the relevant competent ethics committees. Necessary permissions and approvals must be stated in the manuscript.

Ethical approval and consent requirements are assessed according to the type of research. Rather than imposing identical requirements on every study without distinction, the Journal follows applicable regulations and the decisions of competent institutions.

Conflicts of Interest and Funding

Authors, editors, and reviewers must disclose financial and non-financial relationships that could influence, or reasonably be perceived to influence, an evaluation or publication decision.

Conflicts of interest may include financial relationships, consultancy, institutional responsibilities, personal relationships, academic competition, or other circumstances that may affect the impartiality of the editorial or review process.

Authors must disclose research funding sources and explain the role of funding organisations in study design, data collection, analysis, interpretation, manuscript preparation, and the decision to publish. If there is no funding or conflict of interest to declare, this must also be stated.

Editors and reviewers must not participate in the evaluation of manuscripts when a conflict of interest compromises their impartiality. Appropriate safeguards must be implemented to manage such situations. If a conflict of interest is identified after submission or publication, the editor may reassess the manuscript's editorial or publication status.

Use of Artificial Intelligence Tools

Journal ATA recognises the importance of transparency, accuracy, confidentiality, and human accountability in the use of AI-assisted tools in scholarly research. AI tools cannot be listed as authors, and scientific responsibility rests with human authors.

Authors who use AI-assisted tools in preparing a manuscript or conducting research must disclose the tool, its purpose, and the stage of the work in which it was used. Depending on the nature of the use, the disclosure may be included in the acknowledgements, methods, or another appropriate section of the manuscript.

A distinction must be made between limited assistance, such as language editing, and the use of AI in research design, data generation, data analysis, image creation, or scientific interpretation. The scope of disclosure must accurately reflect the tool's contribution to the work.

Authors are responsible for verifying the accuracy, sources, originality, copyright compliance, and potential biases of content generated or transformed using AI. References and citations generated by AI tools must be independently verified. AI tools must not be credited as authors.

Failure to disclose AI use, or inappropriate use of AI, may lead to an ethical review and corrective action, depending on the circumstances.

Editors and reviewers must not upload unpublished manuscripts or confidential information to AI tools that do not provide adequate confidentiality safeguards. AI use in editorial processes must comply with the Journal's confidentiality rules, data-security requirements, and transparency principles. Reviewers must not use AI systems to evaluate manuscript content in ways that violate the Journal's policies or permissions.

Plagiarism, Duplicate Publication, and Research Misconduct

Journal ATA evaluates submitted manuscripts for originality and ethical compliance and addresses plagiarism, duplicate publication, fabrication, falsification, inappropriate citation, improper authorship, and other forms of research misconduct.

Submitted manuscripts may be screened using similarity-detection software and editorial examination where appropriate. Similarity reports are assessed in context, taking into account the source, nature, attribution, and context of the matching material. A similarity percentage alone is not treated as conclusive evidence of misconduct.

When a potential ethical violation is identified, the authors may be asked to provide an explanation and relevant documentation. Depending on the nature and evidence of the misconduct, the manuscript may be rejected, a revision may be requested, or a correction or retraction may be considered after publication. Relevant institutions or competent authorities may be notified where necessary.

Complaints, Appeals, and Allegations of Misconduct

Authors, reviewers, and other relevant parties may submit reasoned complaints concerning editorial decisions, publication practices, or potential ethical misconduct.

Appeals against editorial decisions must be submitted to the Editor-in-Chief within 14 days of notification of the decision, together with the reasons for the appeal and any supporting documentation. If an appeal cannot be submitted within this period, the reason for the delay should be explained. Appeals are considered in light of new scholarly arguments, alleged errors in the evaluation, or claims of procedural irregularity. Acceptance of an appeal does not guarantee publication; an independent reassessment may be arranged where appropriate.

Complaints concerning editors or members of the editorial board are handled, as far as possible, independently, with the individuals concerned excluded from the decision-making process.

Allegations of ethical misconduct are investigated with reference to the relevant COPE guidelines and flowcharts. The process observes impartiality, confidentiality, evidence-based decision-making, and the opportunity for relevant parties to respond.

Corrections, Retractions, and Post-Publication Discussion

If an error, omission, ethical concern, or issue affecting the reliability of a published article is identified, the editors determine the appropriate course of action according to the nature of the concern.

A correction may be issued when an error does not invalidate the main findings of the work. Retraction may be considered when the reliability of the findings is seriously compromised or when the work is associated with ethical misconduct. Where readers need to be informed of serious unresolved concerns, an appropriate editorial notice may be published.

Decisions to correct or retract articles are made to protect the accuracy of the scholarly record. The reason for the action must be stated clearly, and the notice must be linked to the relevant publication. Scholarly criticism and discussion of published work are considered provided they are evidence-based and do not constitute personal attacks.

Publication Policy

Aims and Scope of the Journal

The Journal of Academic Tourism Analysis (Journal ATA) is an international, peer-reviewed, open-access academic journal dedicated to publishing scholarly research in the field of tourism. The journal considers original scientific studies in tourism and related disciplines, including gastronomy, recreation, hospitality, travel, tourism management, tourism economics, and sustainability.

Journal ATA aims to advance theoretical, methodological, and applied research in tourism, foster interdisciplinary scholarly exchange, and facilitate the dissemination of research findings to the international academic community. The journal particularly encourages research on sustainable tourism, sustainable gastronomy, tourism–environment relationships, and interdisciplinary topics consistent with its aims and scope.

The journal follows a Continuous Publication model. Articles that have successfully completed peer review and editorial evaluation are published online as soon as the post-acceptance production process is completed, without waiting for a scheduled issue publication date. Journal ATA accepts manuscripts written in Turkish and English.

Submissions are expected to fall within the journal's aims and scope, demonstrate scientific originality and methodological rigour, and comply with applicable research and publication ethics standards.

Open Access Policy

Journal ATA adopts a Diamond Open Access publishing model that supports free and unrestricted access to scholarly knowledge. All articles published in the journal are made available to readers immediately upon publication, without access fees, subscriptions, or embargo periods.

Published works are distributed under the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 International (CC BY-NC 4.0) licence. This licence permits the sharing, reproduction, and adaptation of published works, provided that appropriate attribution is given and the use is non-commercial.

The journal supports international open-access initiatives aimed at promoting the free circulation and accessibility of scholarly knowledge. Further information on access conditions, licensing, authors' rights, and reuse permissions is provided in the journal's Open Access Policy.

Fee Policy

Journal ATA operates under a non-profit and entirely free publishing model. The journal does not charge authors or their affiliated institutions at any stage of the publication process, including manuscript submission, initial editorial screening, peer review, language editing, typesetting, online publication, and DOI assignment.

The journal does not impose Article Processing Charges (APCs), submission fees, page charges, colour figure charges, supplementary file fees, or fast-track review fees. The evaluation, acceptance, and publication of manuscripts are not conditional upon any payment.

The journal's editorial evaluation, peer-review, and publication activities are conducted on the basis of academic volunteerism. Financial relationships are not permitted to compromise editorial independence or the impartiality of scholarly evaluation.

Further details regarding fees and financial obligations are provided in the journal's Fee Policy.

Peer Review and Evaluation Process

Journal ATA employs a Double-Blind Peer Review system. Under this model, authors' identities are concealed from reviewers, while reviewers' identities are concealed from authors. Appropriate editorial measures are implemented to maintain confidentiality and impartiality throughout the evaluation process.

All submitted manuscripts undergo an initial editorial screening. At this stage, manuscripts are assessed for their relevance to the journal's aims and scope, originality, scientific quality, methodological adequacy, compliance with formatting requirements, and ethical suitability. Manuscripts that do not meet the journal's requirements may be rejected without external peer review or returned to the authors for necessary revisions.

Manuscripts that pass the initial editorial screening are sent to at least two independent reviewers with expertise in the relevant field. Reviewers evaluate manuscripts in terms of scientific contribution, theoretical framework, methodology, consistency of data and findings, justification of conclusions, use of references, and research ethics.

Based on the reviewers' reports, editorial decisions may include acceptance, revision, further evaluation, or rejection. Additional reviewers may be consulted where substantial differences arise between reviewer recommendations or where further expert assessment is required.

For a manuscript to be published, at least two peer-review evaluations must reach a positive recommendation regarding its suitability for publication. Nevertheless, the final publication decision is made by considering both the reviewers' reports and the editorial assessment. Positive reviewer recommendations do not, in themselves, guarantee publication.

Authors are expected to respond to reviewers' and editors' comments with scientific justification and complete the requested revisions within the specified deadlines. Revised manuscripts may be returned to reviewers for further evaluation where necessary.

Editorial decisions are based on scientific merit and the journal's publication criteria. Further information on the peer-review process, evaluation stages, and current timelines is provided in the journal's relevant submission and review guidelines.

Publication Ethics and Similarity Screening

Journal ATA considers compliance with the principles of research and publication ethics a fundamental requirement of the publication process. Submitted manuscripts are evaluated in terms of originality, scientific integrity, appropriate use of sources, and ethical compliance.

Manuscripts may be screened using similarity detection software and editorial assessment. Similarity reports are evaluated by considering not only the numerical similarity percentage but also the source and nature of the similarities, the accuracy of citations, and the context of the text.

Allegations of plagiarism, data fabrication, data falsification, duplicate publication, inappropriate citation, improper authorship, manipulation of the peer-review process, and other forms of scientific misconduct are investigated in light of the available evidence and relevant publication ethics principles.

Where ethical concerns arise, authors may be requested to provide explanations and supporting documentation. Depending on the nature of the suspected violation, the evaluation process may be suspended, revisions may be requested, or the manuscript may be rejected. Appropriate post-publication actions may be taken when issues are identified after publication.

Ethical investigations are conducted with reference to the guidelines of the Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE), applicable legislation, and the journal's Ethical Principles.

Ethics Committee Approval and Participants' Rights

Manuscripts submitted to the journal must comply with applicable legislation regarding ethics committee approvals, research permissions, informed consent, and other ethical documentation required by the nature of the research.

For studies involving human participants, personal data, vulnerable groups, or animals, ethical obligations are assessed according to the type of research and the regulations in force.

Where ethics committee approval is required, the name of the approving committee, approval date, and decision or protocol number must be stated in the manuscript. Where ethics committee approval is not required, the reasons must be clearly explained. Editors may request ethics approval documents, research permissions, or additional explanations where necessary.

The voluntary participation, privacy, protection of personal data, and right to withdraw of research participants must be respected. Authors are responsible for obtaining the necessary permissions for the publication of identifiable personal information, images, or other materials.

Where required ethical approvals are absent, false ethical declarations are provided, or participants' rights are violated, the manuscript may be excluded from consideration, the evaluation process may be suspended, or appropriate editorial action may be taken.

Licensing and Copyright

Works published in Journal ATA are made openly accessible under the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 International (CC BY-NC 4.0) licence.

This licence permits the sharing, reproduction, and adaptation of published works, provided that appropriate attribution is given, a link to the licence is provided, any changes made are indicated, and the use is non-commercial. Commercial uses not permitted under the licence require separate permission from the relevant rights holders.

Authors retain the copyright to their published works and grant the journal a non-exclusive right of first publication. Authors may share their works in other academic venues, provided that the journal is appropriately acknowledged as the original publisher and the applicable licensing conditions are observed.

Authors are responsible for ensuring that third-party materials included in their manuscripts comply with copyright and permission requirements. Appropriate attribution and necessary permissions must be obtained for texts, tables, figures, photographs, and similar content reproduced from other sources.

Further information regarding copyright, reuse conditions, and authors' sharing rights is provided in the journal's Open Access Policy and relevant copyright statements.

Data Sharing and Research Reproducibility

Journal ATA supports transparency, verifiability, and, where appropriate, reproducibility in scientific research. The journal encourages greater accessibility of research data, analysis codes, research materials, and other supporting resources underlying published findings.

Authors may provide information regarding the availability of their research data and any applicable conditions for access or sharing. Where necessary, editors may request additional explanations concerning data collection procedures, analytical methods, or supporting materials to verify research findings.

Data sharing must not conflict with participants' privacy, personal data protection requirements, ethics committee conditions, intellectual property rights, confidentiality obligations, or applicable legislation.

The public disclosure of confidential, sensitive, or personal data is not mandatory. Where data sharing is not possible, the reasons for such restrictions should be explained.

Conflicts of Interest and Editorial Independence

Journal ATA is committed to ensuring that editorial decisions are made independently and impartially on the basis of scientific criteria. Publication decisions are not influenced by advertising, sponsorship, commercial relationships, institutional pressure, or personal interests.

Authors, editors, and reviewers are required to disclose financial and non-financial conflicts of interest that could influence, or reasonably be perceived to influence, evaluation or publication decisions.

Individuals with conflicts of interest must withdraw from the relevant evaluation or decision-making processes, or appropriate arrangements must be made to safeguard impartiality. Where a conflict of interest is identified retrospectively, the editorial process or published work may be re-examined.

Under its current publishing model, the journal does not adopt a publishing approach based on advertising, sponsorship, or direct marketing revenue. Financial and institutional relationships are managed in a manner that does not compromise the independence of scholarly evaluation.

Changes in Authorship and Corresponding Author Responsibilities

The corresponding author is responsible for communication between the journal and the authors throughout manuscript submission, peer review, revision, and publication. The corresponding author must verify that all authors have approved the final version of the manuscript and that all required declarations have been completed.

Requests to add or remove authors or change the order of authorship must be submitted to the editorial office with appropriate justification. Written consent is required from all existing authors and, where applicable, from any individual being added or removed.

Editors evaluate authorship change requests in accordance with scientific contributions, authorship criteria, and publication ethics principles. Additional explanations or supporting documentation may be requested where necessary.

Changes in authorship after manuscript acceptance are exceptional and must be justified. Authorship changes involving published articles are assessed with consideration of the integrity of the scholarly record and any necessary post-publication procedures.

Withdrawal of Manuscripts Under Review and Rejection Decisions

The withdrawal of a manuscript that has not yet been published and remains under evaluation (manuscript withdrawal) is distinct from the retraction of a published article (retraction).

Authors wishing to withdraw a manuscript under review must submit their request to the editorial office through the relevant notification mechanism within the DergiPark system. Withdrawal requests are evaluated and processed in accordance with the editorial workflow implemented through the system.

Authors must not submit the same manuscript to another journal for consideration before the withdrawal process has been completed. Simultaneous submission of the same work to multiple journals is contrary to the principles of publication ethics.

Appeals against editorial rejection decisions must be submitted to the Editor-in-Chief within 14 days of notification of the decision, together with the reasons for the appeal and any supporting documentation. Where an appeal cannot be submitted within this period, an explanation for the delay should be provided.

Appeals are examined in light of evaluation errors, new scientific arguments, or allegations of procedural irregularities. An independent reassessment may be conducted where necessary. Acceptance of an appeal for consideration does not guarantee publication of the manuscript.

Handling Complaints and Appeals

Complaints and appeals concerning the journal's editorial decisions, peer-review processes, publication practices, or potential ethical violations are handled in accordance with the principles of impartiality, confidentiality, and evidence-based assessment.

Submissions should be supported by clear reasons and, wherever possible, relevant information or documentation. Complaints and appeals should be submitted to the appropriate editor or Editor-in-Chief through the journal's official editorial communication channels.

An editor or editorial board member who is the subject of a complaint must not participate as a decision-maker in the assessment of that complaint. Where necessary, an independent editorial evaluation may be conducted or opinions may be sought from relevant institutions.

Submissions are examined in light of the nature of the case and the available evidence. Wherever possible, complainants are provided with a reasoned response following the investigation.

Relevant COPE guidelines and flowcharts are taken into consideration when investigating allegations of ethical misconduct.

Corrections and Retractions of Published Works

Journal ATA evaluates errors, allegations of ethical misconduct, and other issues affecting the scientific reliability of published articles in order to protect the accuracy and integrity of the scholarly record.

A correction may be issued for significant errors that do not invalidate the principal conclusions of a study. A retraction may be warranted where circumstances seriously undermine the reliability of the findings. An Expression of Concern may be published where serious concerns regarding the reliability of a work remain unresolved during an ongoing investigation.

The complete removal of published works from public access is considered only in exceptional circumstances involving compelling legal, safety-related, or similar requirements.

The reasons for post-publication actions are clearly stated, and the relevant notices are linked to the affected articles. Further details concerning the conditions, investigation procedures, notification methods, and preservation of publication records are provided in the journal's Corrections and Retractions Policy.

Digital Archiving and Accessibility of Publications

Journal ATA aims to ensure the long-term accessibility of its published scholarly works and preserve the integrity of its digital publication records.

Articles published in the journal are made openly accessible and digitally archived through the TÜBİTAK ULAKBİM DergiPark publishing infrastructure.

The journal makes use of available digital archiving facilities to support the long-term preservation of published works and maintains practices aimed at sustaining access to publication records.

If the journal suspends or ceases publication, reasonable efforts will be made to preserve access to previously published content within the available technical and institutional resources.

Further information regarding digital preservation, archiving methods, authors' self-archiving rights, and long-term access conditions is provided in the journal's Archiving Policy.

Special Issues and Publication Planning

Journal ATA may publish special issues focusing on scholarly topics consistent with its aims and scope. Information regarding the subject, objectives, submission requirements, evaluation procedures, and publication planning of special issues is provided in the relevant announcements.

Manuscripts submitted to special issues are subject to the journal's general ethical principles, publication policies, and double-blind peer-review requirements.

Special issue editors or guest editors are responsible for disclosing conflicts of interest, safeguarding the impartiality of evaluation procedures, and acting in accordance with scientific standards.

Ultimate editorial responsibility for the preparation and publication of special issues remains with the journal's authorised editors. Special issues are not subject to different or less rigorous standards of publication ethics and peer review than those applied to regular submissions.

Implementation and Revision of Policies

Journal ATA reviews its ethical principles and publication policies in response to developments in scholarly publishing, applicable legislation, international publication ethics standards, and operational requirements.

The journal's publication policies are implemented in conjunction with its separately published Open Access Policy, Fee Policy, Corrections and Retractions Policy, Archiving Policy, and other relevant editorial regulations.

In implementing these policies, reference is made to COPE guidelines, ICMJE recommendations where applicable, relevant legislation, and internationally recognised best practices in scholarly publishing.

The journal may update its policies when necessary. Updated policies are made accessible through the journal's official publishing platforms.
